column2: An omen in a blazing direction is called direction-blazing; in a village (forest animals), in a forest (village animals), or a censured tree,
and in an inauspicious place is to be known as place-blazing, best of twice-born; act-blazing is declared as one whose act is unfit for its own species;
cry-blazing is said to be one of broken, terrible sound; species-blazing is to be known as one that feeds only on flesh.
The calm is declared from the blazing, by all the distinctions with care; the mixed one by mixtures; its fruit and non-fruit should be told.
Cow, horse, camel, ass, dog, myna, house-lizard, sparrow, bhasa, tortoise and the like are called village-dwellers;
goat, sheep, parrot, elephant, boar, buffalo and crow are declared both village and forest; all others are forest-ranging.
Cat and cock are village animals and also forest-ranging; knowledge of those two arises always from difference of form.
Gokarna, peacock, chakravaka, ass, harita, crow, kulaha, kukkubha, hawk, jackal, wagtail and monkey,
shataghna, sparrow, shyama, chasha, hawk, kalinjala, partridge, shatapatra and pigeon — these three;
khanjarita, datyuha, parrot, jivaka, cock, Bharadvaja and sarnga — these are to be known as day-goers.
Vagurī, owl, sharabha, heron, hare, tortoise, lomasika and pingalika are said to be night-ranging.
Swans, deer, cat, mongoose, bear, serpents, wolf, enemy of lions, lion, tiger, camel, village boar, humans,
swavit, bull, jackal, wolf, cuckoo, crane, horse, loin-cloth-wearing men and iguana are both-ranging.
At a force's march, all those going in front in flocks are declared victory-bringing; those behind cause death.
When a crow, having gone from the house, calls standing in front, it announces the king's insult; on the left, a quarrel at meals;
on a journey its sight is praised, or on the left side of the body. A peacock with broken sound announces robbery by thieves.
A deer in front of one who has set out, Rama, may take life. Bear, rat, jackal, tiger, lion, cat, ass
in reverse, Rama, and an ass with a distorted voice; the kapinjala on the left is best, and likewise standing on the right;
from behind it has a censured fruit; the partridge is not praised. Deer, boars and spotted deer, being on the left and then on the right,
always bring wealth; the reverse are censured. Bull, horse, jackal, tiger, lion, cat and ass
are to be known as granters of the desired when going from right to left. Jackal-woman, shyamanana, chuchchu, pingala, house-lizard,
sow, cuckoo and masculine-named ones on the left; feminine-named: bhasa, karusha, kapishrikarna, chhitkara;
kapishrikarna, pipyika, ruru and hawks on the right. Mention of jati, iksha, snake, hare, boar and iguana is auspicious;
then their sight is not wanted; reversed for monkey and bear. An omen that does the work and is powerful, for one who has set out, daily,
its fruit should be told by the wise on that very day. Children seeking food and those attached to enmity are considered thus,
and those on the border within are to be known as fruitless, twice-born. A jackal-woman with one, two, three or four cries is fortunate;
with five and likewise six she is declared unfortunate; with seven fortunate; beyond that fruitless.
One producing horripilation in men and fear in vehicles — fire-flame, sun-faced — is to be known as increasing fear.
When a sarnga is first seen in an auspicious place one should say good; for a man for a year; and in inauspicious, good likewise;
so a man should see the sarnga on the first day; and by one's own being so the year's fruit should be known.
In beating shadow, limb, vehicle, sandals, umbrella, cloth and the like, death; in worshipping them, honor; in doing what is desired, good.
A crow making the return of an absent one, going and coming at the door; one throwing red burnt substance in the house announces fire;
one placing red in front announces bondage; yellow substance, gold or silver, Bhargava,
whatever substance it brings, one should declare the gain of that; what substance it carries away, one should declare the loss of that.
In front, wealth would be gained when it vomits raw flesh; land gained when it throws clay; great kingdom when it offers jewels.
A crow favorable to one who is going is safe and fit for the work; but the contrary should not be known as accomplishing the purpose, it brings fear.
One approaching in front crying causes the journey's failure. A crow on the left is remembered as fortunate; on the right, destroying wealth;
on the left going with the grain is best; the right is remembered as middling; moving against the grain on the left prohibits going.
Having gone into the house, it announces the intended purpose of the journey. One standing on one foot looking at the sun brings fear;
dwelling in a hollow it makes great ill. A crow on barren ground is not good; but one with mud-marks is praised;
a crow with a mouth full of impure things accomplishes all aims. Other birds too are to be known like the crow, son of Bhrigu.
Dogs on the left in the camp destroy Brahmins. In Indra's place of a king, in the city-gate of the town-lord,
barking inside the house of the house-lord it would mean death. Whose left side it smells, that brings success of purpose;
the right side and the left arm bring fear; coming facing the traveler it causes the journey's failure;
obstructing the way, it says of thieves on the road, Bhargava. Bone in mouth: no gain and sin; likewise a rope or rag in mouth;
with sandals in mouth it is fortunate, also with mouth full of meat. An inauspicious thing in the mouth and hair are inauspicious likewise;
one who urinates and goes in front of someone — fear for him; one who urinates and goes for someone, a good place or tree,
and an auspicious object, is for his success. Jackals and the like, Rama, are to be known like the dog.
A cry of cows without cause is to be known as fear for the master; at night it is for fear of thieves; distorted, for death;
a bellowing bull at night for the master's welfare; a bull set free gives the king victory.
Cows eating fearlessly, and given or one's own, who have lost affection for their calves, are considered abortive;
beating the ground with feet, wretched, frightened, they bring fear; wet-bodied, bristling, with clay on the horns, auspicious.
All this the knowing one should declare for buffaloes and the like. Mounting by another of a saddled horse,
sitting in water and rolling on the ground are not wanted; sleeping without cause brings calamity to the horse;
sudden dislike of barley and modaka is not praised; blood from the mouth and trembling are not praised.
Playing with pigeons or mynas, it would foretell death. With tears in the eyes and licking the feet with the tongue, for destruction;
likewise scratching the earth with the left foot, or sleeping on the left side by day, is not auspicious;
a once-urinating and sleepy-faced one means fear; if it does not allow mounting or goes home backward,
it announces obstruction of the journey, touching its left side; neighing at enemy warriors, touching the foot, brings victory.
If an elephant goes mating in a village it would destroy the country; a female elephant that has given birth and is in rut, for the king's end;
if it does not allow mounting or goes home backward, or the elephant lets out rut, it becomes a king-killer.
One that treads the left foot with the right is auspicious; and wipes the right tusk with the trunk.
A bull, horse or elephant gone to the enemy's army is inauspicious. By excessive rain in broken clouds the army would meet destruction;
by adverse planets and stars and by wind from the front, at the time of a journey or in war, the fall of umbrella and the like is fear;
men glad and planets in the favorable direction are the sign of victory; by crows the warriors' defeat, by flesh-eaters the destruction of the circle.
East, west, northeast, north and the beloved direction are auspicious.
At an omen and the like, going on an auspicious day for victory, remembering Hari. At the end of the contemplation of the mandala I shall tell what is to be done: protection of the king.
Lord, minister, fort, treasury, army, ally and country — the kingdom is called seven-limbed.
One should destroy those who obstruct the seven-limbed kingdom. By the king prosperity should be made in all circles.
Here one's own circle is the first circle. Its neighbors are to be known as enemies of the circle.
The one attached is to be known as friend; beyond is the enemy's friend; then the friend's friend; then the friend's friend's enemy.
This has been told in front; hear from me also the rear: Parshnigraha behind, then Akranda is said;
then another is Asara, called Akranda-asara. For the conqueror, one joined with enemies, and one released, twice-born,
here too no certainty can be stated, best of men. One capable of subduing and favoring is called the neutral.
One who is capable of subduing and favoring all is called the indifferent, a powerful king.
